newsitem.title: USA: Senator says sawmills win 3 years' timber supply.
newsitem.headline: Senator says sawmills win 3 years' timber supply.

text.p: Louisiana-Pacific Corp. won a three-year federal guarantee that timber will be funneled from the Tongass National Forest to two of the company's Alaska sawmills, U.S. Sen. Frank Murkowski said Monday.

Murkowski, an Alaska Republican who chairs the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, said the deal had been struck between a Louisiana-Pacific unit, Ketchikan Pulp Co., and the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
"I'm very pleased to announce today that an agreement has been reached that will provide timber for three years to the two sawmills," Murkowski said in his speech to the Alaska legislature in Juneau.

"This is really good news for southeast Alaska, especially Ketchikan and Metlakatla." The two towns, in the southern part of Alaska's rain forest-covered southeast panhandle, are the sites of the Louisiana-Pacific sawmills.
Murkowski last fall held up passage of a sweeping parks and conservation bill in an unsuccessful attempt to win an extension of Ketchikan Pulp's long-term contract for Tongass timber.

Murkowski and other Alaska politicians failed in their bid to add 15 years to the 50-year contract, now scheduled to run out in 2004. But they did secure a promise from the Clinton administration to negotiate a deal to help keep the sawmills open.
Without the contract extension and other concessions, Louisiana-Pacific said, it would have been forced to close its money-losing Ketchikan pulp mill.
